title: The house of al-Arqam
hookLine: early Muslims meet in secret at a young man's house to learn and pray

cards: A door near the hill of Safa, in the middle of Mecca. People come to it one at a time, not in a crowd: a merchant, a freed slave, a young man from a powerful clan.
Inside, someone is reciting new verses slowly, so they can be learned by heart. Others are bowing in prayer. Outside, the city goes about its business, and the door stays shut.

teach.h: A YOUNG MAN OPENS HIS HOUSE.
teach.b: Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam was one of the early believers, from the clan of Makhzum, and the sirah writers describe him as young when he came to Islam. He had a house near Safa, and he opened it.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, used it as a meeting place for the believers: a place to teach, to recite what had come down, and to pray together out of sight. Why out of sight?
The sirah tells that the early Muslims at first went out to the valleys around Mecca to pray, and that at least once they were found there and mocked, and it came to blows. A house was safer.
So for a stretch of time, this small house became something like a hidden school. Look at who could sit together there. Outside, in Mecca, a person's clan decided much of how they were treated.

teach.h: FROM THE VALLEYS TO A ROOM.
teach.b: Inside al-Arqam's house, a freed man and a merchant of Quraysh could sit in the same room and learn the same verses from the same teacher.

teach.h: A FREED MAN BESIDE A MERCHANT.
teach.b: Sirah writers later called it Dar al-Arqam, the house of al-Arqam, and some of them tell of people who came to Islam within its walls.
And what made it possible was one young man saying, use my house.
He didn't preach in the street. He offered a room near Safa, with a door that could be shut.

how: Muslims remember Dar al-Arqam in sirah study as the house where the early believers met to learn and pray; Muslims still gather in small study circles to learn the Qur'an together.

practice: Make a small quiet place wherever you are: a closed door, a parked car, a bench under a tree, or just your eyes closed, and let the noise of the day stay on the other side.
If you pray, pray here simply, the way you know how; if not, breathe, and listen to what a small, quiet space lets you hear.

wordCard.voice: Al-Arqam. A young believer from the clan of Makhzum, whose house near Safa became a hidden school for the earliest Muslims. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the house of al-Arqam; dar means house or home.

carryVoice: Your line: a hidden school. One young man, one room, one door that could be shut. Seven hundred thirty days, and counting.
